newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia launches new $480 million port.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia launches new $480 million port.

text.p: Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad officially launched on Tuesday Malaysia's 1.2 billion ringgit ($480 million) West Port, expressing hope that it will steer the future of the nation's shipping industry.

The port, which officials hope will become a regional shipping hub with its status as duty-free port, will require the effort of all local shippers and relevant government departments to succeed, Mahathir said.

"It is a national duty," the prime minister was quoted as saying by the national Bernama news agency as he launched the West Port, located at the Pulau Indah island off Port Klang, Malaysia's premier port located in central Selangor state.
The West Port, with 11 wharves in operation, is the third port close to Malaysia's federal capital after the North Port and South Port, both controlled by the Port Klang.
The West Port begin operating on a small-scale in September 1994 before undergoing major expansion.
The privately-administered port currently has 11 berths to serve fifth generation post-Panamax vessels of above 5,000 TEUs (20-foot equivalent units) and up to 80,000 tonnes displacement.

Officials said the number of berths would reach 32 over the next five years and the port would be able to handle liquid bulk, cement, liquefied petroleum gas, dry bulk, break bulk and container cargo.
They said the port and its supporting facilities were estimated to have cost 1.2 billion ringgit to date.
West Port executive chairman G. Gnanalingam was quoted as saying by the Business Times newspaper on Tuesday that another 1.5 billion ringgit was needed over the next five years to expand the port.

Mahathir said the absence of a large international port in Malaysia previously led to most of the country's goods being exported through ports in other countries, resulting in an increase in the services deficit.

"If the insurance industry and CIF (cost in freight) and FOB (free on board) are arranged in a manner that can benefit us, that is CIF for imports and FOB for exports, we might be able to reduce our services account deficit," he added.
Mahathir said the government would do its utmost for the West Port but added that local shippers and the rest of the private sector had to cooperate.

"If you give in once in a while to your friendly competitor, in the long run it will benefit you and it will benefit the nation. Whatever benefits the nation must eventually benefit you," Mahathir said.
